identifications.body:
S. physalifolium is actually endemic to South America. Outside of South America is a very similar-looking species, S. nitidibaccatum (formerly a variety of S. physalifolium but now recognised as a distinct species).

S. nitidibaccatum has large calyxes on flowers and when fruiting, the calyxes expand to partially cover the fruits. It also has black u or v shaped markings at the base of the corollas. In contrast, S. villosum lacks the markings on the corollas and has smaller calyxes that do not expand in fruit.
